title: A walk waits for the panel instead of racing it
goal: Scripted walks fail every so often and pass on the very next run of the same build, always the same shape: the walk looks for a control in the right hand panel and the control is not there yet, or presses one and the press lands where the control used to be. Four separate walks did this in the last three days. A walk that answers differently twice in a row is worse than no walk, because a real break looks exactly like the flake, and every false failure costs a runner a task on the feature in focus. Give a walk a way to wait for the panel to settle instead of guessing a delay, so these stop.
notes:
Reproduced 2026-09-12 on a clean tree.

effects-say-their-reach-walk: failed 1 run in 3 standalone.
  Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/effects-say-their-reach-walk.json --no-build
  status failed, [51 expect] FAILED: the control called "Switch" in "Shadow" reads "Shadow, on", not "Shadow, off"
  and in a suite run, the same walk at a different step: [34 expect] FAILED: the control called "Switch" in "Shadow" reads "Shadow, on for 1 of 2", not "Shadow, off for 1 of 2"

effects-room-for-the-one-you-opened-walk: passed 3 of 3 standalone, failed inside
  Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build effect
  with [32 expect] FAILED: the control called "Twist" in "Border" reads "Border, shut", not "Border, open"
  Step 29 is the second of two presses on the Border's chevron, and step 28's comment already says a full second is needed there because folding a pane slides every heading below it. That points at a press landing mid relayout: the walk waits a fixed time, and when the panel is slower than the wait the press lands where the chevron was.

Both misses are the same shape: a press that finds its target's old position. Worth looking at whether a press should settle the layout before it lands, rather than every walk guessing a wait long enough.

log.note: merged find-out-why-a-walk-passes-on-its-own-and-fails and find-out-why-the-effects-plus-goes-nameless-whil into this task; added the 2026-09-13 sweep evidence, three of thirteen failures reproduced as passing on their own

Reproduced before touching anything. `Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build effect` -> 11 passed, 2 failed (border-effect-walk, glow-effect-walk), both at a press step with "the control X is not where a person could click it". Ran border-effect-walk 5 more times back to back: failed 4 of 5. The latest sweep (queue/sweep/latest.json, 397/404) names the same two, and four of its seven failures are that one message.

Adversarial review of the idea, before building. (1) The task frames this as a race, and half of it is not: border-effect-walk step 30 needs the panel scrolled 46pt. Inserting a `reveal` step in a scratch copy makes the whole walk pass, exit 0. The second Border pushes its Width slider below the fold, and the walk was written when the panel was shorter. Nothing is racing there: the walk is asking to press something a person would have to scroll to first. (2) So the shortest thing that delivers the value is not a new wait step for authors to remember, it is a press that behaves like a person: look, scroll to it if it is not in reach, then press. That retires `reveal` as a thing anyone has to remember and kills the whole "not where a person could click it" class at once. (3) The decorative version of this task would be a new `waitForControl` step. There already is a `waitFor`, and adding a second spelling of waiting is how a walk author gets a choice they should not have to make. Cut it. (4) The one thing auto-scrolling could hide is a real regression where the panel grew so tall the control fell off. It cannot hide it: the scroll is logged with the distance, and a control nothing can bring into reach still fails with the message it fails with today.

Cause, one sentence per half. THE RACE: `settle()` judges the app quiet from two signals, and one of them is dead for most of a walk. MainThreadMeter.install() is only called by press/drag/scroll steps, so every `wait` before the first press reads mainBusy 0 over ZERO passes and goes quiet after ~0.1s no matter what the app is doing (log line, verbatim: `[2 wait] 1.0s asked, quiet after 0.10s; mainBusy -2.6ms over 0 passes, longest 0.0ms`). That is exactly a walk reading the dock while it is still being built. THE INHERITANCE: a walk inherits whatever the probe was last left in and only forgets what it declares, 225 of the 405 walks declare nothing, and `experiments.release` is not in the net at all, so a probe left on Current runs every walk against the wrong app while still reporting pass/fail as if it were Next (seen here: wiping the probe defaults put it on Current and border-effect-walk then failed at step 6 with a panel that has no effects list in it).

Built and verified. A press now: keeps looking for its control for up to 2s; scrolls it into reach if the dock has it below the fold; and waits for the box to hold still AND the app to be quiet over the same stretch before the mouse events go out. `expect` and `panelMenu` keep looking the same way. The MainThreadMeter is installed from step zero, so a `wait` is no longer blind for the first half of a walk, and a slice the run loop never came back in counts as busy rather than quiet. probe-app.sh pins experiments.release=next before each launch. `"forget": ["all"]` is the one word for a clean machine.

One false start worth writing down: the first version of the settle-before-press never once read the app as quiet, because reading the panel walks the whole view tree and that work was being charged to the app as main thread busy. MainThreadMeter.exclude() already exists for exactly this and just was not being called. With it called, the walk that failed 2 of 8 passed 8 of 8.

Acceptance runs against the final build. effects-say-their-reach-walk 10 of 10. text-style 6/6 five runs. style swatch 16/16 five runs. border effects panel 33/33 (three runs here, two more on the same build earlier). layers 8/8 four of five; the one failure was layers-lazy-rows-walk at step 270, which turned out not to be the press race at all: scrollPanel asked for -4000pt in ONE turn, and a lazily built list only has as much length as it has built, so the turn stopped at a content size that was still growing and the step after it looked for the bottom row of a list that was a third scrolled. scrollPanel now goes in rounds, asking for what is left until a round moves nothing; that walk went 2 of 3 to 4 of 4.

Acceptance 10 verified rather than assumed. A scratch copy of border-effect-walk pressing a control that does not exist ("Slider" in "@border, Wibble") still fails, with exactly the message it failed with before: `no row called "@border, Wibble" is in the panel, so there is nothing on it to press; the steady names on screen: @border, @border.1, @fill`. The whole walk took 9s, so the two seconds of patience is a small cost on a real break.

Acceptance 9, why the Add Effect plus went nameless, written up in docs/design/playtest-harness.md. The plus has no words on it, so a walk opens it by the name SwiftUI hands the underlying NSPopUpButton through .accessibilityLabel, which is what PlaytestPanelMenu.title(of:) reads. SwiftUI pushes that label on as part of reconciling the representation and the AppKit control exists before that happens, so for the first frames of a relayout the plus is there, right size, right tooltip, and answering to no name. The panelMenu step keeps looking now.

Final runs, stated plainly. MET: acceptance 1 (cause named per half), 2 (written up in docs/design/playtest-harness.md, with the release pinned and `forget: ["all"]` added), 3 (every press, expect, panelMenu and scrollPanel now waits for its control rather than sleeping a guessed number), 5 (text-style 6/6 five runs), 6 (style swatch 16/16 five runs), 8 (effects-say-their-reach-walk 10 of 10), 9 (the nameless plus is waited for and the reason is written down), 10 (verified by breaking a walk on purpose: same message, 9s), 11 (two follow-ups filed). NOT MET: acceptance 4 and 7. border effects panel ran 33/33 five times and then failed once on the sixth; layers ran 8/8 five times but an earlier run came in at 6 of 8, one of those being align-layers-walk at 185s with no done.json, which is a walk that never finished rather than one that failed. Both remaining misses landed in runs where the machine was saturated. The flake is much rarer, not gone, and saying otherwise would be the exact thing this task exists to stop.
